verses.english: Numbered Discourses 10.45
5. Abuse
Entering a Royal Compound
“Mendicants, there are ten drawbacks to entering a royal compound.
What ten?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, rājā mahesiyā saddhiṁ nisinno hoti.
verses.english: Firstly, a king is sitting with his chief queen
when a monk enters.

verses.pali: Mahesī vā bhikkhuṁ disvā sitaṁ pātukaroti, bhikkhu vā mahesiṁ disvā sitaṁ pātukaroti.
verses.english: When the queen sees the monk she smiles, or when the monk sees the queen he smiles.
So the king thinks:
‘They’ve done it for sure, or they will do it.’
This is the first drawback of entering a royal compound.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, rājā bahukicco bahukaraṇīyo aññataraṁ itthiṁ gantvā na sarati:
verses.english: Furthermore, a king has many duties, and much to do. He has sex with one of the women but doesn’t remember.
She gets pregnant from that.
So the king thinks:

verses.pali: ‘na kho idha añño koci pavisati, aññatra pabbajitena.
verses.english: ‘No-one else has entered here, except for that monk.
Could this be the monk’s doing?’
This is the second drawback of entering a royal compound.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, rañño antepure aññataraṁ ratanaṁ nassati.
verses.english: Furthermore, a gem is lost somewhere in the royal compound.
So the king thinks:

verses.pali: ‘na kho idha añño koci pavisati, aññatra pabbajitena.
verses.english: ‘No-one else has entered here, except for that monk.
Could this be the monk’s doing?’
This is the third drawback of entering a royal compound.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, rañño antepure abbhantarā guyhamantā bahiddhā sambhedaṁ gacchanti.
verses.english: Furthermore, secret deliberations in the royal compound are leaked outside.
So the king thinks:

verses.pali: ‘na kho idha añño koci pavisati, aññatra pabbajitena.
verses.english: ‘No-one else has entered here, except for that monk.
Could this be the monk’s doing?’
This is the fourth drawback of entering a royal compound.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, rañño antepure pitā vā puttaṁ pattheti putto vā pitaraṁ pattheti.
verses.english: Furthermore, in a royal compound, a father longs for their son, or a son longs for his father.
They think:

verses.pali: ‘na kho idha añño koci pavisati, aññatra pabbajitena.
verses.english: ‘No-one else has entered here, except for that monk.
Could this be the monk’s doing?’
This is the fifth drawback of entering a royal compound.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, rājā nīcaṭṭhāniyaṁ ucce ṭhāne ṭhapeti.
verses.english: Furthermore, the king promotes someone to a higher position.

verses.pali: Yesaṁ taṁ amanāpaṁ tesaṁ evaṁ hoti:
verses.english: Those who are upset by this think:
‘The king is close to that monk.
Could this be the monk’s doing?’
This is the sixth drawback of entering a royal compound.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, rājā uccaṭṭhāniyaṁ nīce ṭhāne ṭhapeti.
verses.english: Furthermore, the king demotes someone to a lower position.

verses.pali: Yesaṁ taṁ amanāpaṁ tesaṁ evaṁ hoti:
verses.english: Those who are upset by this think:
‘The king is close to that monk.
Could this be the monk’s doing?’
This is the seventh drawback of entering a royal compound.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, rājā akāle senaṁ uyyojeti.
verses.english: Furthermore, the king dispatches the army at the wrong time.

verses.pali: Yesaṁ taṁ amanāpaṁ tesaṁ evaṁ hoti:
verses.english: Those who are upset by this think:
‘The king is close to that monk.
Could this be the monk’s doing?’
This is the eighth drawback of entering a royal compound.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, rājā kāle senaṁ uyyojetvā antarāmaggato nivattāpeti.
verses.english: Furthermore, the king dispatches the army at the right time, but orders it to turn back while still on the road.

verses.pali: Yesaṁ taṁ amanāpaṁ tesaṁ evaṁ hoti:
verses.english: Those who are upset by this think:
‘The king is close to that monk.
Could this be the monk’s doing?’
This is the ninth drawback of entering a royal compound.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, rañño antepuraṁ hatthisammaddaṁ assasammaddaṁ rathasammaddaṁ rajanīyāni rūpasaddagandharasaphoṭṭhabbāni, yāni na pabbajitassa sāruppāni.
verses.english: Furthermore, in the royal compound there is a trampling of elephants, horses, and chariots, as well as arousing sights, sounds, smells, tastes, and touches that do not befit a monk.
This is the tenth drawback of entering a royal compound.

verses.pali: Ime kho, bhikkhave, dasa ādīnavā rājantepurappavesane”ti.
verses.english: These are the ten drawbacks of entering a royal compound.”
